title: Rust: Array Operations
description: Transform arrays using iterator methods like map, filter, and fold.

steps.title: Map: Double Values
steps.description: Create an array `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` and use `.iter().map()` to double each value. Collect into a Vec and print it.
hints: `.collect()` gathers the results into a collection.

steps.title: Filter: Even Numbers
steps.description: From `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]`, use `.iter().filter()` to keep only even numbers. Print the result.
hints: `.filter()` keeps elements where the closure returns true.
Note the dereference `*x` since filter gives references.

steps.title: Fold: Sum
steps.description: Use `.iter().fold()` to sum all numbers in `[10, 20, 30, 40]`. Print the result.
hints: `fold` starts with an initial accumulator (0) and applies the closure.

steps.title: Chain Map and Filter
steps.description: From `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]`, first filter odds, then map each to its square. Print the result.
hints: Filter first, then transform with map.

steps.title: Any and All
steps.description: Check if any number in `[1, 3, 5, 7, 9]` is even using `.iter().any()` and if all are odd using `.iter().all()`. Print both results.
hints: `.any(|x| x % 2 == 0)` returns true if any element matches.
`.all(|x| x % 2 != 0)` returns true if all elements match.
Even check should be false, All odd should be true.

verification.failureMessage: Print the results of any even and all odd checks.
